The Desolation of the Jews for Their Sins Foretold in the Valley of Hinnom; the Symbol of Breaking a Bottle.</title> <div sID="gen17824" type="x-p"/> Referred by Maurer, &c., to the beginning of Zedekiah's reign.<div eID="gen17824" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17825" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10008"/><hi type="bold">1. bottle--</hi>Hebrew, bakuk, so called from the gurgling sound which it makes when being emptied.<div eID="gen17825" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17826" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ancients--</hi>elders. As witnesses of the symbolic action (<reference osisRef="Jer.19.10">Jr 19:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.8.1">Is 8:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.8.2">2</reference>), that the Jews might not afterwards plead ignorance of the prophecy. The seventy-two elders, composing the Sanhedrim, or Great Council, were taken partly from "the priests," partly from the other tribes, that is, "the people," the former presiding over spiritual matters, the latter over civil; the seventy-two represented the whole people. <div eID="gen17826" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 19 Jr 19:1-15 . The Desolation of the Jews for Their Sins Foretold in the Valley of Hinnom; the Symbol of Breaking a Bottle. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10009"/><div sID="gen17827" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10009"/><hi type="bold">2. valley of the son of Hinnom--</hi>or Tophet, south of Jerusalem, where human victims were offered, and children made to pass through the fire, in honor of Molech.<div eID="gen17827" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17828" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">east gate--</hi>Margin, "sun gate," sunrise being in the east. Maurer translates, the "potter's gate." Through it lay the road to the valley of Hinnom (<reference osisRef="Josh.15.8">Jos 15:8</reference>). The potters there formed vessels for the use of the temple, which was close by (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.19.10">Jr 19:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.19.14">14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.18.2">Jr 18:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.11.13">Zec 11:13</reference>). The same as "the water gate toward the east" (<reference osisRef="Neh.3.26">Ne 3:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Neh.12.37">12:37</reference>); so called from the brook Kedron. Calvin translates, as English Version and Margin. "It was monstrous perversity to tread the law under foot in so conspicuous a place, over which the sun daily rising reminded them of the light of God's law." <div eID="gen17828" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10013"/><div sID="gen17837" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10013"/><hi type="bold">6. no more ... Tophet--</hi>from Hebrew, toph, "drum"; for in sacrificing children to Molech drums were beaten to drown their cries. Thus the name indicated the joy of the people at the fancied propitiation of the god by this sacrifice; in antithesis to its joyless name subsequently.<div eID="gen17837" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17838" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">valley of slaughter--</hi>It should be the scene of slaughter, no longer of children, but of men; not of "innocents" (<reference osisRef="Jer.19.4">Jr 19:4</reference>), but of those who richly deserved their fate. The city could not be assailed without first occupying the valley of Hinnom, in which was the only fountain: hence arose the violent battle there. <div eID="gen17838" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10018"/><div sID="gen17845" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10018"/><hi type="bold">11. as one breaketh a potter's vessel--</hi>expressing God's absolute sovereignty (<reference osisRef="Jer.18.6">Jr 18:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.2.9">Psa 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.30.14">Is 30:14</reference>, Margin; <reference osisRef="Lam.4.2">La 4:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.9.20">Ro 9:20</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.9.21">21</reference>).<div eID="gen17845" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17846" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cannot be made whole again--</hi>A broken potter's vessel cannot be restored, but a new one may be made of the same material.
